splices.old: The wave equation is nearest-neighbor, so the cubic lattice is bipartite: even sites couple only to odd sites and vice versa. This bipartite structure is a property of the dynamics (range-1 coupling on a hypercubic graph), not of the partition.
splices.new: The wave equation is nearest-neighbor, and the cubic lattice $\mathbb Z^3$ is bipartite, as is a periodic quotient of it whose period vectors all have even coordinate sum: even sites couple only to odd sites and vice versa (the parity of $n_1+n_2+n_3$ is well defined on the quotient exactly then, and a period vector of odd coordinate sum closes a walk of odd length). A quotient with such a vector, for example a torus of odd side, carries no checkerboard. On the lattices that carry it, this bipartite structure is a property of the dynamics (range-1 coupling on a hypercubic graph), not of the partition.
